Average Instagram organic reach is 3.2%. That's from Socialinsider's 2026 benchmark study — 872,075 posts analysed between January 2025 and August 2026. Down 14% year over year.

On a 2,000-follower account, a normal post reaching 130 people is not a failure. It is the average.

I'm telling you this because the number nobody gives you is the one that stops you quitting. Most people starting out think their content is broken. It usually isn't. The distribution got tighter for everyone, and every platform with ads has a reason to keep it that way.

Two useful things follow from it:

→ Smaller accounts actually reach a bigger share of their own audience than big ones. 1k–5k accounts average 6.65%. 100k–1M average 3.50%. Being small is an advantage you will never have again.

→ If you need predictable volume, organic alone won't give it to you. That's not failure, that's arithmetic.
